title: heap-buffer-overflow: vdbeRecordCompareInt THREE_BYTE_INT
live_proof: fuzz-corpus diff: the image reproduces on stock 3.22.0 under host ASan as heap-buffer-overflow in vdbeRecordCompareInt at sqlite3.c:77204
arena_bytes_why: 1 MiB on every arm. Five of the eight spatial cases are forced here by reachability -- at 262144 cases 21, 22 and 23 exhaust memsys5 before the defect (pcache1AllocPage dereferences the NULL that 3.22.0 does not check), 29 returns SQLITE_NOMEM, and 00 takes a different path -- so the same value is declared for all eight to keep the arms comparable. Measured 2026-10-17; this is also the value every recorded virtual reading was taken at, while CheriBSD had been running 262144.
object: the serialized record vdbeRecordCompareInt decodes an integer field from. The read is aKey = &((const u8*)pKey1)[*(const u8*)pKey1 & 0x3F], an offset of up to 63 bytes taken from the record's own header byte and never checked against nKey1, followed by a read of up to eight bytes at aKey chosen by serial_type
lifetime_ender: not a lifetime defect: a corrupt record header claims a field wider than the record, and the decode reads past it
shape: read past the end of the record
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator, with a reconstructed trigger -- see case 24 for why the SQL had to be re-derived and why it must be replayed one statement per process. note: Re-measured 2026-10-16. THE SUBLET CELL CHANGES FROM NOT-DETECTED TO DETECTED, and this is the only case in the corpus where that arm was recorded as missing. The physical rows explain their silence as follows, quoted from results/matrix.tsv: 'The case’s own return code says why nothing was detected: s0_rc=11, SQLITE_CORRUPT -- the trigger’s database image is rejected'. That reasoning does not hold, and the two virtual arms show why on one image and one statement. Without Sublet: open_rc=0, then s0_rc=11, NOTRAP done, RETURNED -- the over-read COMPLETES, the decode returns garbage, and SQLite's own corruption check rejects the result afterwards. With Sublet: open_rc=0, then the fault, cause=28 in vdbeRecordCompareInt, before s0_rc is ever printed. So SQLITE_CORRUPT is a CONSEQUENCE of the out-of-bounds read, not a sign that the read never happened, and the defect is reached on exactly the statement whose return code was taken as evidence that it was not. That also settles the base cell: virtual-malloc is a genuine reached-and-silent, since the Sublet arm establishes reachability on the same statement and the same image. The CheriBSD cell was recorded as a NO-READING on that date and is NOT one; the correction is 2026-10-17. The hits=0 came from this arm compiling its own copy of the case under ports/sqlite/cheribsd/cases/, which ran PRAGMA integrity_check BEFORE the trigger -- on a corrupt image that makes SQLite reject the trigger with SQLITE_CORRUPT, so the defect was unreachable. build-corpus-cheri.sh now takes the case program from the corpus, as build-virtual.py does. Re-measured from the corpus source the arm MISSES: s0_rc=11 as on virtual-malloc, and site 65 reports hits=3 witnesses=3, all kind=OOB, through a tag=1 capability bounded to the whole 262144-byte arena. The defect itself is an unchecked offset taken from the data: aKey = pKey1 + (*pKey1 & 0x3F), up to 63 bytes in, never compared against nKey1, then up to eight bytes read at aKey according to serial_type. Site 65 prints pKey1, nKey1, the header byte, serial_type, aKey and whether the widest read already passes the end. One stale cross-reference is corrected: fidelity pointed at case 34, which does not exist
fault_sites_why: Host ASan, running the same case source on stock 3.22.0, reports the invalid access in vdbeRecordCompareInt (live_proof); that run is independent of the Capstone arms and predates them.
